title: Solubility nonlinearity gives a 5.7 umol/kg mixing limit on density 26.5 for source densities 26.3-26.7 in a grid test
abstract: We test if nonlinear oxygen solubility can explain the North Pacific AOU rise without a change of oxygen use. We allow any mixture that conserves salt and heat and ends on sigma0 26.5. Refined source grids give a maximum two-period mixing-term rise of 5.675 umol/kg for source densities 26.3-26.7 and salinity 32-36 g/kg. A separate linear program checks the extreme. All 10,938 regional GLODAPv2.2023 bottles in this density band have salinity inside 33-35.5. The published total western AOU rise is 12.55 (7.258-16.77) umol/kg. Numerical capacity is 45% of its point value. Source densities 26.1-26.9 permit 10.677 and overlap that interval. Solubility nonlinearity has limited capacity within the narrow class, but a broad source range weakens the test. These are finite-grid bounds, not a continuous certificate or a formal statistical rejection of regression estimates. Mixing of different oxygen-use histories, source gas disequilibrium and general transport remain open.
